This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #44913
* #44912
* #44904
* #44901

## Motivation

Shared-expert fusion determines expert weights, router widths and capture buffers for the lifetime of a loaded model. Resolving the count in each MoE block and passing it through intermediate constructors duplicates that decision; storing target/draft copies in process flags adds a separate restoration protocol.

Resolve the layout once, keep its related quantities together, and expose the active model's configuration during construction and execution.

## Modifications

- Add frozen `SharedExpertsConfig`, owned by the loader-created model. It contains the resolved fusion decision, fused expert count and Waterfill policy. Its `num_shared_topk_slots` property is zero when Waterfill writes the shared slots later, otherwise the fused count.
- Expose that object through the runtime-only `get_model().shared_experts` leaf. The loader scopes construction; runner boundaries scope eager execution, warmup, capture and replay, including direct draft graph paths. Existing bag overrides restore nested and exceptional exits. Model replacement reads the replacement model's configuration.
- TopKConfig and HashTopK retain the same immutable object. Selecting another model cannot resize existing layers or graphs. Remove the fusion/count active/speculative flags and their manual save/restore.
- Resolve fusion only when an entry class declares both its veto and `num_fusable_shared_experts` capability. Model families and wrapper entry classes supply the appropriate hooks. MoE blocks and weight loaders read the resolved count at construction.
- Size routed-experts capture from the supplied model's configuration, including wrapper entry models, independently of the ambient binding.
- Retain `FusedMoE`'s count argument with its shape inputs. Qwen-family gated shared-expert fusion remains block-local.
- Update the runtime-context skill and behavior tests for target/draft alternation, nesting, failures, model replacement, direct capture and compiled reads.

### API changes

`TopK.top_k` counts routed experts only and its `num_fused_shared_experts` argument is removed. HashTopK parameters after `num_experts` are keyword-only. Model integrations declare `num_fusable_shared_experts` alongside their fusion veto instead of overriding `determine_num_fused_shared_experts`. TopKConfig receives `shared_experts`, with the ordinary slot count exposed as a read-only property.

## Validation

At `b500124929`, with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, FlashInfer 0.7.2 and Transformers 5.19.0:

- 51 CPU test files pass: MoE/Waterfill/scaling/HashTopK, model capability and wrapper policy, routed capture, target/draft scope isolation, runner lifecycle, runtime namespace and raw-input/resolution checks.
- Four H200 CUDA routing files pass: `test_topk_padded_region.py`, `test_fused_append_remap_per_rank_shared_slots.py`, `test_topk_renormalize_degenerate.py`, `test_jit_grouped_topk.py` (31 cases, 7 backend-specific skips).
- `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` with Inductor and CUDA Graph capture/replay pass for ordinary fusion, Waterfill and unfused configurations: three graphs, nine replays with changed inputs and different ambient configurations.
- GLM-4.7-Flash on 2× H200, BF16, TP2, Triton attention/MoE, decode CUDA Graph batches 1/2/4, routed-experts capture enabled: four sequential greedy requests match PR1 `6a5c963f49` exactly in tokens and expert routes. One of two batched requests varies between repeated PR1 runs; the repeated PR1 run matches PR2 on all six requests. This is limited smoke coverage, not an accuracy benchmark.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks pass on every changed file.

At the updated head `faaf4bb4e6`, after integrating #44912 `b7f88f502e`:

- Five CPU files pass all 83 cases: scaling, draft construction isolation, Waterfill EPLB, routed-experts capture and fusion capability policy.
- The CUDA append/remap/runtime-routing file passes all nine cases. The registered Triton fused-MoE file passes its full 96-configuration matrix on one H200.
- The previous head's Triton test fails in all 96 configurations because TopK construction reads an unpublished model namespace. The fixture now publishes and restores context in `setUp`, before construction, and removes publication from the numerical reference. Constructor-only scaling fixtures also restore their scope before returning.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks pass. Versions for these checks: torch 2.14.1+cu130, sgl-kernel 0.4.10, FlashInfer 0.7.2, Triton 3.8.0, Transformers 5.19.0.

Not covered: full-model Waterfill or fused-draft E2E, distributed DeepEP/MegaMoE E2E, AMD, NPU or XPU runtime execution.

## CI fixture follow-up at `5214d477ec`

The [ROCm 10 MI35x job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39124404687/job/117666744625) failed at `faaf4bb4e6` because `test_deepseek_v4_amd_tp4.py::_moe_stub` bypasses `DeepseekV2MoE.__init__` and omitted `routed_scaling_factor_fused_in_topk`. The stub now supplies that construction state. The other five test files in that partition passed. This fixes the test fixture; production executable behavior is unchanged.

On one H200, the original fixture reproduces the same AttributeError with the AITER epilogue flags forced; after repair, all four normal/dual-stream and shared-TP1 combinations pass through the actual forward methods. This checks the Python fixture/epilogue contract, not native ROCm collectives or graph replay. The complete AMD TP4 file still needs CI validation.

The kernel comparison now covers normalization and explicit folding independently; the complete standalone router test file passes all 52 cases on one H200. Its stale normalization explanation and CUDA JIT parity claim are corrected. The CUDA counterpart retains its existing unnormalized shared-weight behavior; caller search found tests and benchmarks, with no serving caller.

TopKConfig documents its total ordinary output width and the global AITER absolute shared coefficient versus the standard-path multiplier. Eager/fused subtest labels include the folding mode. Duplicate ordinary model-context scopes and a derived routed-count property remain optional follow-ups. Applicable pre-commit hooks pass. No native AMD rerun or model accuracy result is claimed for this follow-up.

The repaired stack is #44901 `cdf052beb7` → #44904 `beb15ea999` → #44912 `720d6dbef4` → #44913 `5214d477ec`.

## Attention draft-runner CI follow-up at `bb8c02ce3b`

The [H100 job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39126305260/job/117672499853) failed at `5214d477ec` in the MLA Triton draft graph test: the shared attention test kit's `_TinyDraftModel` bypasses loading and lacked `shared_experts_config`, which `BaseRunner.model_context` now requires. The adjacent `_EagleDraftExtendForward` test model had the same omission. Both pure-attention model constructors now carry an explicit empty `SharedExpertsConfig`, matching the model-owned layout contract. The production runner remains unchanged.

On one H200 (torch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2, Triton 3.8.0), the original source produces three missing-attribute errors across the two existing draft decode/extend test methods. After repair, the complete MLA Triton file passes nine tests and the complete dense Triton file passes ten, including EAGLE decode/extend and Frozen-KV capture/replay. Applicable pre-commit checks pass. The earlier image-output equality assertion passed on retry and was not the terminal job failure; no base/head attribution is claimed for it.

Only #44913 changes in this follow-up. The full CI partition has not been rerun locally; these results cover the existing attention graph integration files.
